requirements.en: State how far you agree or disagree.
requirements.vi: Nêu mức độ đồng ý hoặc không đồng ý.

requirements.en: Support your position with two clear reasons.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Television use reduces face-to-face talking.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Watching TV can make people feel alone.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Watching TV can make people feel alone.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The first point argues that television does not worsen communication because people can still use video calls to connect with relatives and share news.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The first point argues that television does not worsen communication because people can still use video calls to connect with relatives and share news.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The second point suggests that TV is not a problem because people can use the screen for other activities, such as watching movies and discussing them with friends.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The second point suggests that TV is not a problem because people can use the screen for other activities, such as watching movies and discussing them with friends.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The first body paragraph argues that TV viewing reduces the need for face-to-face communication, leading to poorer social skills.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The first body paragraph argues that TV viewing reduces the need for face-to-face communication, leading to poorer social skills.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The second body paragraph argues that excessive TV viewing causes feelings of isolation and weakens community bonds.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Television does not reduce the time for people to connect with loved ones.

keyArguments: Television reduces face-to-face interaction, leading to weaker interpersonal relationships.
The reliance on virtual communication through phones and other devices has eroded the quality of family bonds.

plan.focus: Analyze the impact of television on communication between friends and family, focusing on the reduction of quality time spent together and the shift towards virtual communication.
keyArguments: Television reduces face-to-face interaction, leading to weaker interpersonal relationships.
The reliance on virtual communication through phones and other devices has eroded the quality of family bonds.
